text: The Beginner project at Driftwood Outdoor Apparel solved a real problem for one stakeholder: Theo Bryant moved the storefront app's static assets to Azure Blob Storage and the app itself onto a single Azure VM, for IT Manager Priya Suresh. It held up, but it's still exactly one bad week away from a problem.

A few months later, Priya introduces Theo to Casey Lindqvist, Driftwood's newly hired VP of Engineering. Casey inherited what Theo built and doesn't want every future project to be another one-off that only Theo can rebuild from memory.

Priya and Casey come to Theo together with four deliverables: containerize the storefront app with Docker, provision Azure infrastructure with Terraform, build a CI slash CD pipeline so deploys aren't manual, and add AWS as a backup target for the app's data.

That fourth item is scoped on purpose. Azure stays home. AWS exists only so Driftwood's data has a copy somewhere else if Azure ever had a very bad day. Nothing about the running application itself moves to AWS.
Next lesson reconciles what might look like two different priorities, Priya's and Casey's, into one single project plan before any code gets written.
